title: Something of Value
summary:
As I've previously reported,
Andrew is a professional investor who focuses on making long-term investments in what the world
calls growth companies, and especially technology companies. Growth stocks have meaningfully outperformed value for the last 13 years. My extensive discussions with Andrew led me to
conclude that the focus on value versus growth doesn't serve investors well in the fast-changing
world in which we live.

positions.commentary: Howard Marks notes that a well-known value investor held Amazon stocks two decades ago because they looked like value to him, even though they are acknowledged winners today.

thesis: This episode contains a single specific claim regarding Amazon, noting that a well-known value investor held the stock two decades ago because it appeared to offer value at the time, despite the company now being acknowledged as a market winner.

claims.claim: Howard Marks notes that a well-known value investor held Amazon stocks two decades ago because they looked like value to him, even though they are acknowledged winners today.
claims.quote: I once asked the well-known value investor how he could hold the stocks of fast-growing companies companies like Amazon. Not today, when they're acknowledged winners, but rather two decades ago. His answer was simple. They looked like value to me.
